differences.aspect: Checkpoint spacing vs. the actual room size
differences.design_x: Design X's prototype sketch places checkpoints at normalized coordinates like (0.25, 0.56) and (0.45, 0.7), which in a 6 x 6 m room works out to roughly 1.2-1.9 m between stops, and the build plan only says to keep a 1.2 m corridor and 0.6 m edge margin.
differences.design_y: Design Y states in the options step that the 5 stops are about 2-3 m apart, repeats this in the prototype decisions, and carries 'about 2-3 m apart' into the final layout brief.
differences.evidence: Options step: Design Y mechanics says 'เส้นทางเดินวงกลม 5 จุด ห่างกันประมาณ 2–3 เมตร' (a 5-stop circular route with stops about 2-3 m apart); Design X mechanics lists the 5 stops with no spacing. Prototype step: Design Y decisions include 'จุดแวะห่างกันประมาณ 2–3 เมตร'; Design X sketch coordinates imply shorter hops. Build step: Design Y layout brief says 'about 2-3 m apart'; Design X layout brief has no spacing figure.

differences.design_x: Design X promises story text of no more than two lines in the HUD but never specifies sign size, colour contrast, or mounting height.
differences.design_y: Design Y specifies large cream-on-dark-wood signboards at chest-to-eye height in the prototype decisions and HUD, and repeats 'large cream-on-dark-wood signboards at chest to eye height' in the build plan; it also playtests whether players can read signs without bending.
differences.evidence: Prototype step: Design Y decisions include 'ใช้ป้ายสั้นตัวใหญ่สีครีมบนพื้นไม้สีเข้ม ตัดสีชัด' (short signs, large letters, cream on dark wood, high contrast) and HUD lists 'ป้ายชื่อจุดแวะตัวใหญ่ตัดสีชัด' and text 'ที่ระดับสายตาถึงระดับอก' (at eye-to-chest level); test question 3 asks whether signs are readable 'โดยไม่ต้องก้มหรืองอตัวมาก' (without much bending). Design X HUD only says 'เรื่องสั้นไม่เกินสองบรรทัด' (story of at most two lines).

differences.aspect: Fallback for players with unsteady gait
differences.design_x: Design X acknowledges in the options risks that walking a loop in a small space may cause dizziness and offers only 'หยุดพักได้ทุกจุด' (can rest at every stop).
differences.design_y: Design Y's options risks flag that unsteady players may need a seated computer-based alternative, the prototype decisions commit to offering that alternative and keeping rest chairs outside the route, and the test questions watch for players reaching for walls or staff for balance.
differences.evidence: Options step: Design Y risk 'ผู้ที่เดินไม่มั่นคงอาจยังต้องการทางเลือกเล่นบนคอมพิวเตอร์แบบนั่งเล่น' (unsteady players may need a seated computer option). Prototype step: Design Y decision 'เสนอทางเลือกเล่นบนคอมพิวเตอร์สำหรับผู้ที่เดินไม่มั่นคง' and test question 'มีใครเอื้อมหากำแพงหรือเจ้าหน้าที่เพื่อทรงตัวหรือไม่' (does anyone reach for walls or staff to balance). Design X has no equivalent in any step.

differences.design_x: Design X's prototype decisions award 100 points per checkpoint plus a 300-point finish bonus 'บวกโบนัสเวลา' (plus a time bonus), which conflicts with its own no-time-pressure pillar, and the final build plan silently drops scoring entirely, leaving the rules inconsistent between steps.
differences.design_y: Design Y's prototype decisions state points are computed from stops and time but never displayed during the walk, the HUD explicitly lists 'ไม่มีนาฬิกาจับเวลา ไม่มีคะแนน' (no timer, no score), and the build plan repeats 'no in-play score or timer display'.
differences.evidence: Prototype step: Design X decision 'แตะจุดได้จุดละ 100 คะแนน จบได้ 300 คะแนนบวกโบนัสเวลา' vs. its pillar 'ไม่มีเวลาจำกัด'; Design Y decision 'ระบบให้คะแนนตามจุดกับเวลา แต่ไม่แสดงคะแนนระหว่างเดินเพื่อไม่ให้รู้สึกถูกกดดัน'. Build step: Design X rules contain no scoring at all; Design Y layout brief says 'no in-play score or timer display'.

differences.design_x: Design X places audience zones on both left and right sides of the room in the prototype sketch and orients the dessert-stall stop toward the right-side audience with the final portal visible to both sides, matching the brief's 'friends seated on chairs around the room'.
differences.design_y: Design Y concentrates spectators on the south side near the finish in the sketch and build plan, which serves the warm ending but covers the 'around the room' seating less evenly.
differences.evidence: Prototype step: Design X sketch has 'เพื่อนๆ นั่งชมด้านซ้าย' (x 0.08) and 'เพื่อนๆ นั่งชมด้านขวา' (x 0.92); Design Y sketch has a single audience zone at (0.5, 0.94). Build step: Design X 'orient the dessert-stall stop toward the right-side audience and keep the final portal visible to both sides'; Design Y 'Friends sit outside the play area around the room, especially along the south side'. The brief says 'เพื่อนๆ นั่งเก้าอี้รอบห้อง' (friends on chairs around the room).

differences.design_x: Design X's climax is the Thai dessert stall followed by a wooden bridge over a canal vignette; evocative, but the ending is a private walk through the exit portal.
differences.design_y: Design Y builds to an old-radio corner (music/news from the past is a strong memory trigger for 60-75 year olds) and places the finish portal beside the friends' seating so the session ends in shared storytelling, which the storyboard and spectator plan both reinforce.
differences.evidence: Prototype step: Design Y storyboard climax 'เสียงจากวันวาน' (sounds from the past) at the 'มุมวิทยุเก่า' (old radio corner) and end beat 'เล่าสิ่งที่นึกถึงให้เพื่อนฟัง' (tell friends what you remembered); pillar 3 'จบแล้วอยากเล่าและฟังเรื่องราวร่วมกับเพื่อนๆ'. Design X storyboard climax is 'ขนมหวานในความทรงจำ' (dessert stall) and the end is 'รับข้อความจบเรื่อง แล้วถอดแว่น' (receive ending text, remove headset).

differences.design_x: Design X specifies a 1.2 m minimum corridor and 0.6 m edge margin in the options step and repeats both in the build plan, plus 'no objects requiring the player to look up while walking'.
differences.design_y: Design Y specifies the same 1.2 m corridor and 0.6 m boundary margin in the build plan and adds 'never a void' floor and chest-height signs to avoid bending.
differences.evidence: Build step: Design X 'at least 1.2 m wide... at least 0.6 m from the play-area edge'; Design Y 'at least 1.2 m wide... at least 0.6 m from the play-area boundary'. Options step: Design X environment_fit states the same 1.2 m / 0.6 m figures.

differences.design_x: Design X's flow spaces five stops across 0:30-3:40 with a 4:00 headset-off, a comfortable pace for short hops.
differences.design_y: Design Y's flow covers five stops across 0:20-3:30 ending at 4:00; slightly tighter per-stop time but with longer walks between stops, roughly equivalent overall.

differences.aspect: Quality and honesty of the alternative options
differences.design_x: Design X's battle option ('ผู้พิทักษ์ร้านไม้เก่า') includes sword combos, shielded enemies and a boss for first-time elderly VR users, and its own risk note admits it conflicts with the safety constraint; its tactics option uses three chess piece movements (rook, knight, bishop).
differences.design_y: Design Y's battle option is deliberately de-escalated (slow weak enemies only, no shield units, no giant boss, no hazard rain) and its tactics option simplifies to rook-only movement with a slower 3.5 s guard cadence and verified solvable boards, showing more disciplined adaptation to the brief even in the rejected options.
differences.evidence: Options step: Design X battle mechanics 'การฟันเป็นชุดสามครั้ง... เพิ่มศัตรูถือโล่... เจ้าตัวใหญ่' and risk 'ขัดกับความต้องการปลอดภัยมากและไม่ต้องรีบ'; Design Y battle mechanics 'ใช้เฉพาะศัตรูตัวเล็กที่เดินช้าและอ่อนแอ ไม่มีศัตรูถือโล่ ไม่มีเจ้าตัวใหญ่'. Design X tactics uses 'เรือ... ม้าและบิชอป' with guards every 5 s; Design Y tactics uses 'หมากเรือเดินแนวตรง' with guards every 3.5 s and 'ทุกกระดานถูกสร้างและตรวจสอบว่าแก้ได้'.

differences.design_x: Design X gives a six-colour palette with evocative Thai names and a detailed key-art prompt naming the dessert stall and canal.
differences.design_y: Design Y gives a five-colour palette and a comparably detailed key-art prompt that additionally encodes the signboard and route requirements.
differences.evidence: Prototype step: both provide palette hex codes, prompt_style strings, and first-person Quest 3 key-art prompts of similar specificity.

improvements: For Design X: resolve the scoring contradiction — either drop the time bonus or state explicitly that scores are never shown during play, and keep the build plan consistent with whichever choice is made.
For Design X: add explicit stop spacing (2-3 m) so the 5-stop loop fills the 6 x 6 m room instead of clustering stops ~1.5 m apart.
For Design X: specify sign size, contrast, and mounting height, and add a seated/desktop fallback for unsteady walkers.

For Design Y: distribute spectator sightlines beyond the south side so friends seated on the north and side chairs also get a clear view of at least one stop, matching the 'around the room' seating in the brief.
For both: state a maximum continuous standing/walking duration before a mandatory rest prompt, since 4 minutes of standing can still be long for some 60-75 year olds.
summary: Both sessions converge on the same correct concept — a gentle 5-stop nostalgic market walk in a loop with no timer and no hazards — and both carry it consistently through prototype and build plan with the same core safety numbers (1.2 m corridor, 0.6 m edge margin). Design Y is stronger where it matters most for this audience: it spaces stops 2-3 m apart so the walk actually fills the 6 x 6 m room (Design X's sketch implies ~1.2-1.9 m hops), specifies large high-contrast chest-height signage, plans a seated fallback for unsteady walkers, keeps scoring invisible so it cannot create time pressure (Design X introduces a time bonus in the prototype and then drops scoring silently in the build plan), and ends the session beside the friends with an old-radio memory trigger. Design X is slightly better at distributing spectator sightlines around the room and marginally richer in palette detail, but these do not offset Design Y's gameplay, readability, and consistency advantages.
why: Design Y wins on the aspects that most affect these specific players: walk distances that match the room and the 'light exercise' goal, readable signage for ageing eyes, a concrete fallback for unsteady gait, internally consistent no-pressure scoring across all three steps, and a socially warm ending. Design X's advantages (two-sided spectator coverage, slightly richer palette) are real but secondary, and its time-bonus scoring contradicts its own safety pillar before disappearing from the build plan.
x_weaknesses: Checkpoint spacing never stated; sketch coordinates imply stops only ~1.2-1.9 m apart in a 6 x 6 m room, weakening the light-exercise goal.
Prototype introduces a time bonus ('บวกโบนัสเวลา') that contradicts the no-time-pressure pillar, and the build plan then drops scoring entirely — an unresolved inconsistency between steps.
No signage readability specification (size, contrast, height) for elderly players.
No fallback for players with unsteady balance beyond 'rest at any stop'.
Rejected options are less adapted to the brief (sword combos, boss, three chess piece types) and the battle option's own risk text admits the mismatch.
y_weaknesses: Spectator coverage is concentrated on the south side near the finish, under-serving friends seated elsewhere 'around the room' as the brief describes.
Flow timing is slightly tighter per stop (first two stops within the first ~1:20) which could feel rushed if a player lingers, though there is no enforced timer.
The seated computer alternative is mentioned in options and prototype decisions but is not carried into the final build plan or spectator/staff plan.
